classification.difficultyReason: Part f requires identifying equal base angles in the whole isosceles triangle and transferring them into two right triangles to calculate the split apex angles.

content.prompt: Find the value of each pronumeral, giving reasons.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle ABC with matching ticks on AB and AC.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; angle ABC=alpha; angle BAC=beta; angle ACB=65 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=65^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$).

$\begin{align*}\beta+65^\circ+65^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=50^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Right isosceles triangle with equal AB and BC and a right-angle mark at B.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC; angle ABC=90 degrees; angle ACB=gamma.

answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\gamma$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$).

$\begin{align*}2\gamma+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\gamma&=90^\circ\\\gamma&=45^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Triangle FGH with FG=GH and GH extended left to T.
spec.mathematics: T,G,H are collinear; angle TGF=132 degrees; angle GFH=beta; angle FHG=alpha.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=\beta$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle FGH$).

$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta&=132^\circ\\2\alpha&=132^\circ\\\alpha&=66^\circ\end{align*}$

Exterior angle of $\triangle FGH$. Hence $\beta=66^\circ$.

$\angle QPR=\alpha$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle PQR$).

$\begin{align*}2\alpha+108^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=72^\circ\\\alpha&=36^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle PQR$.

spec.description: Triangle FGH with matching ticks on FG and FH and a 60-degree apex angle.
spec.mathematics: FG=FH; angle GFH=60 degrees; angle FGH=alpha; angle FHG=beta.

answer.worked:
$\alpha=\beta$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle FGH$).

$\begin{align*}2\alpha+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=60^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle FGH$. Hence $\beta=60^\circ$.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle ABC with perpendicular AM to BC; the apex angle is split into alpha and beta.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; M lies on BC; AM perpendicular BC; angle ABC=48 degrees; angle BAM=alpha; angle MAC=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither unknown apex angle is supplied.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\alpha+48^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=42^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle ABM$.

$\angle ACB=48^\circ$ (base angles of isosceles $\triangle ABC$).

$\begin{align*}\beta+48^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=42^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of $\triangle ACM$.
